ukoksq.q: The sign shown is a priority sign
ukoksq.why: The Give Way (Dare precedenza) sign belongs to the priority signs, together with STOP and the priority road sign.

1o2tdtb.q: The sign shown requires you to give way to vehicles coming from both the right and the left
1o2tdtb.why: The sign makes you give way to traffic on the crossing road from both directions, right and left.

1vn5ucz.q: The sign shown requires you to give way to vehicles travelling on the road that crosses yours
1vn5ucz.why: At a Give Way sign you must yield to vehicles on the crossing road.

1g6bb6o.q: The sign shown is placed on a secondary road that does not have right of way
1g6bb6o.why: The sign stands on the minor road, which has no priority over the road it meets.

7764eo.q: The sign shown is found on acceleration lanes used to join the motorway
7764eo.why: On acceleration lanes (corsie di accelerazione) merging traffic must yield to vehicles already on the motorway, so this sign is used there.

3bl8cm.q: On extra-urban roads, the sign shown is preceded by the ADVANCE WARNING OF GIVE WAY sign
3bl8cm.why: Outside built-up areas the Give Way sign is announced by its advance warning sign, placed before the junction.

1g74kml.q: The sign shown warns you to slow down considerably and, if necessary, stop
1g74kml.why: The sign tells you to slow down a lot and stop if needed in order to let approaching vehicles pass.

b3u68t.q: With the sign shown you do not have to stop at the junction if, by slowing down, you can see that no vehicles are coming from either the right or the left
b3u68t.why: Give Way does not require a stop: if you slow down and see no traffic from either side, you may proceed.

u51k3a.q: The sign shown is a prescription sign
u51k3a.why: Priority signs, Give Way included, are prescription signs (segnali di prescrizione) because they impose a behaviour.

1akxi09.q: The sign shown requires you to give way to vehicles travelling on the road you are entering
1akxi09.why: When you enter a road past a Give Way sign you must yield to the vehicles already on it.

zmj2sz.q: The requirement of the sign shown, when combined with a traffic light, applies when the light is flashing yellow
zmj2sz.why: When the light flashes yellow, the priority sign applies; with a normally working signal, the signal prevails.

1xp753u.q: The sign shown is found on the link ramps used to join the motorway
1xp753u.why: On slip roads joining the motorway you must give way to traffic already on it, so Give Way is posted there.

1i61oxt.q: The sign shown requires maximum caution to avoid accidents
1i61oxt.why: The sign demands great caution at the junction, where you must yield to prevent collisions.

xmxvj4.q: The sign shown may be preceded by the PRIORITY ROAD sign
xmxvj4.why: Give Way is announced by its own advance warning; the priority road sign (diritto di precedenza) marks the main road instead.

ryftc6.q: The sign shown is used on roads that have right of way
ryftc6.why: The sign is used on minor roads, which do not have right of way.

3yhk0v.q: The sign shown is normally placed 150 metres before the junction
3yhk0v.why: The sign stands at the junction itself; 150 m applies to its advance warning outside built-up areas.

1j0s9oo.q: Along motorways, the sign shown is placed at a distance greater than 150 m
1j0s9oo.why: The sign is placed at the point where you must yield, not more than 150 m away.

p81uwn.q: The sign shown requires you to stop before entering the junction
p81uwn.why: Give Way does not force a stop if the road is clear; only the STOP sign makes a stop compulsory.

1y32zct.q: The sign shown is found only on urban roads
1y32zct.why: The sign is used on all roads, urban and extra-urban, including motorways and slip roads.

1etvw2s.q: The sign shown is a generic danger sign
1etvw2s.why: It is a priority sign, not a danger sign: it requires you to give way.

tyys80.q: With the sign shown you must give way to the left only to trams and emergency vehicles
tyys80.why: Give Way requires yielding to all vehicles on the crossing road, from right and left, not only trams and emergency vehicles.

vrr95n.q: The sign shown may be preceded by the ADVANCE WARNING TO STOP AND GIVE WAY
vrr95n.why: The advance warning for STOP belongs to the STOP sign; Give Way has its own separate advance warning.

1t2gol6.q: Along motorways, the sign shown is placed 150 metres from the service area
1t2gol6.why: On motorways the sign is placed where traffic merges onto the carriageway, unrelated to service areas (aree di servizio).

1aepvem.q: The sign shown announces that you must come to a halt before entering the junction
1aepvem.why: The sign announces no compulsory halt: it requires giving way, stopping only if necessary.

1jz9lnr.q: The sign shown is found only on extra-urban roads
1jz9lnr.why: Give Way is used on both urban and extra-urban roads.

1y664tw.q: The sign shown requires you to stop at the transverse stop line and give way to other vehicles
1y664tw.why: STOP requires a halt at the transverse stop line (striscia di arresto) and then giving way to other traffic.

1k1iri6.q: The sign shown requires you to stop and give way before entering the junction
1k1iri6.why: STOP always requires a full stop, then giving way, before you enter the junction.

1hebmcd.q: The sign shown requires you to stop at the junction and give way to the right and to the left
1hebmcd.why: You must stop at the junction and yield to traffic from both right and left.

18ttdu4.q: The sign shown requires you to stop at the junction even when there is a flashing yellow traffic light
18ttdu4.why: With a flashing yellow light the priority signs apply, so the STOP obligation remains.

1m0w873.q: The sign shown is found at the junction with a road that has right of way
1m0w873.why: STOP is placed on the minor road where it meets a road with right of way.

1qivzkm.q: The sign shown is generally found at junctions with poor visibility
1qivzkm.why: STOP is normally used at junctions with poor visibility or high danger, where simply giving way is not enough.

1mh3at0.q: Outside built-up areas, the sign shown is preceded by its advance warning sign
1mh3at0.why: Outside built-up areas STOP is announced by its advance warning sign.

b33z5a.q: The sign shown is normally used at particularly dangerous junctions
b33z5a.why: STOP is normally used at particularly dangerous junctions or where visibility is insufficient.

1r3bhz6.q: The sign shown may be found at a level crossing
1r3bhz6.why: STOP may be placed at a level crossing (passaggio a livello), where a halt is required.

1iujdlm.q: The sign shown announces the obligation to stop and give way in alternating one-way sections
1iujdlm.why: STOP announces nothing and applies at junctions; alternating one-way sections (sensi unici alternati) have their own signs.

un6hxh.q: The sign shown requires you to stop at the customs crossing
un6hxh.why: STOP is a priority sign; customs posts use a different, specific sign.

1jxhph5.q: The sign shown requires you to stop only if you meet other vehicles at the junction
1jxhph5.why: The stop is always compulsory, even when no other vehicles are approaching.

1hkwlky.q: The sign shown requires you to stop to give way only to vehicles coming from the right
1hkwlky.why: After stopping you must give way to vehicles from both right and left.

1e01dqg.q: The sign shown is normally placed 150 metres before the junction
1e01dqg.why: STOP stands at the junction itself; its advance warning, outside built-up areas, is 320 m before.

uihxr6.q: The sign shown requires you to stop because transit is prohibited
uihxr6.why: STOP requires a halt to give way, not because passage is forbidden; you proceed once the road is clear.

19y80ir.q: The sign shown announces that you must stop at the junction even if the traffic light is green
19y80ir.why: The sign is not an advance warning, and a working traffic light prevails: on green you may go.

16zyp7.q: The sign shown announces an obligation to stop at a checkpoint set up by the police
16zyp7.why: Police checkpoints use the HALT-POLICE (ALT-POLIZIA) sign; STOP concerns priority at junctions.

yzmw6m.q: The sign shown requires you to stop only if other vehicles are approaching
yzmw6m.why: STOP requires a stop in every case, even when the road is clear.

1n95n7o.q: The sign shown is a prescription sign
1n95n7o.why: The advance warning of give way is a prescription sign, not a danger sign.

1b3buah.q: The sign shown is an advance warning to give way both to the right and to the left
1b3buah.why: It warns of a coming Give Way sign, which applies to traffic from both sides.

1z0t9lf.q: The sign shown announces that a GIVE WAY sign will follow
1z0t9lf.why: With its distance panel, the sign announces the Give Way sign ahead.

1byq6c3.q: The sign shown indicates the distance from the junction where we must give way
1byq6c3.why: The panel shows how far ahead the junction is where you must give way.

1h7tmz3.q: The sign shown warns you to slow down so you can stop if there are vehicles you must give way to
1h7tmz3.why: The warning tells you to slow down so you can stop if vehicles require you to yield.

1mzbc7j.q: The sign shown may announce a T-junction where you must give way
1mzbc7j.why: The warning may announce a junction, including a T-junction, where you must give way.

1ed2m0j.q: The sign shown is placed on a road that does not have right of way
1ed2m0j.why: The warning is placed on the minor road, which will have to yield.

r69lto.q: The sign shown is an advance warning to stop and give way
r69lto.why: It warns of Give Way; the advance warning for STOP carries the word STOP on its panel.

nev2r2.q: The sign shown announces the distance to the next STOP sign
nev2r2.why: The sign announces a Give Way sign, not a STOP sign.

enre5w.q: The sign shown indicates the distance to the junction where we will have to stop
enre5w.why: It shows where you will have to give way, with no compulsory stop if the road is clear.

110k96g.q: With the sign shown you must stop at the next junction
110k96g.why: The warning does not require a stop: it tells you to slow down and be ready to give way.

x44hr2.q: The sign shown announces a junction where the rule is to give way only to the right
x44hr2.why: It announces a Give Way junction, where you yield to traffic from both right and left.

6is8b9.q: The sign shown announces a three-light traffic signal 320 metres ahead
6is8b9.why: It warns of a Give Way sign, not of traffic lights, which have their own warning sign.

ipor9t.q: The sign shown is an advance warning to stop and give way
ipor9t.why: The sign with STOP and a distance is the advance warning to stop and give way.

16jy6y7.q: The sign shown announces a STOP sign 320 metres ahead
16jy6y7.why: The panel shows that a STOP sign lies 320 metres ahead.

zey5h.q: The sign shown announces that you must stop at the next junction and give way to the right and the left
zey5h.why: It warns of a junction where, at the STOP sign, you stop and give way to traffic from both sides.

xkezae.q: The sign shown announces that you must stop 320 metres after the sign and give way
xkezae.why: The warning means the stop and give-way obligation comes 320 metres further on.

6bpaba.q: The sign shown urges you to slow down because a junction is near where you must stop and give way
6bpaba.why: The warning urges you to slow down because a STOP junction is approaching.

1uor1nv.q: The sign shown is a prescription sign
1uor1nv.why: The advance warning of STOP is a prescription sign, belonging to the priority signs.

1hhll4u.q: The sign shown requires only slowing down and, if necessary, giving way at the junction 320 metres ahead
1hhll4u.why: The sign concerns STOP, which always requires a halt; slowing down alone is not enough.

ybv64k.q: The sign shown is placed 320 metres from the GIVE WAY sign
ybv64k.why: The sign is placed 320 m from the STOP sign, not from the Give Way sign.

wnmrd0.q: The sign shown is found only on urban roads
wnmrd0.why: The 320 m advance warning is used outside built-up areas, on extra-urban roads.

1ybpfi6.q: The sign shown announces a customs barrier
1ybpfi6.why: It announces a STOP sign, not a customs barrier, which has its own signs.

cq0wtc.q: The sign shown may announce a motorway toll booth
cq0wtc.why: The sign announces a STOP; toll booths (caselli) have their own signs.

l253zv.q: The sign shown is placed before the HALT-POLICE sign
l253zv.why: The sign comes before a STOP sign, not before the HALT-POLICE sign.

g8kvz9.q: On meeting the sign shown you must stop and then stop again after 320 metres
g8kvz9.why: The sign itself requires no halt: you stop only at the STOP sign that follows.

7n8jwj.q: The sign shown is a danger sign
7n8jwj.why: It is a prescription (priority) sign, not a danger sign.

3s9m9e.q: The sign shown announces a junction where the general rule of giving way to the right applies
3s9m9e.why: The crossroads sign announces an unmarked junction where the general rule applies: give way to the right.

1weqce3.q: The sign shown requires you to proceed at a particularly moderate speed
1weqce3.why: The sign calls for particularly low speed, since at the junction traffic from the right has priority.

a6pofa.q: The sign shown announces a junction where you must give way to the right
a6pofa.why: It announces a junction with no priority signs: you yield to vehicles from the right.

1vqdq46.q: The sign shown is a priority sign
1vqdq46.why: It is listed among the priority signs because it flags a junction with right-hand priority.

11lcyx6.q: The sign shown is not found on the stretch of road that has right of way
11lcyx6.why: The sign is not placed on a road with right of way, which has its own sign.

1qddb59.q: The sign shown warns of a guarded level crossing with barriers
1qddb59.why: A guarded level crossing has its own sign; this one shows a junction with right-hand priority.

8c4dt9.q: The sign shown comes before the GIVE WAY sign
8c4dt9.why: It announces junctions with no signed priority, so it does not precede the Give Way sign.

1gy50r3.q: The sign shown comes before the STOP sign
1gy50r3.why: It announces junctions where right-hand priority applies, so it does not precede STOP.

1jg5t6v.q: The sign shown is normally placed no more than 50 metres from the junction
1jg5t6v.why: Outside built-up areas danger signs are normally placed about 150 m before the junction.

ytb1dm.q: On motorways, the sign shown is placed at a distance greater than 250 metres
ytb1dm.why: On motorways danger signs are placed about 250 m ahead, not more.

ksyvz4.q: The sign shown announces the ST ANDREW'S CROSS sign
ksyvz4.why: This is itself the crossroads sign; the St Andrew's cross (croce di Sant'Andrea) belongs to level crossings.

1mzvhqj.q: The sign shown requires you, at narrowings, to give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction
1mzvhqj.why: This sign requires you to give way to oncoming vehicles at a narrowing or alternating one-way section (senso unico alternato) where only one line of vehicles can pass.

vx2vbt.q: The sign shown warns in advance, where there are roadworks, that you must give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction
vx2vbt.why: Where roadworks narrow the carriageway, this sign requires you to give way to oncoming vehicles, because only one line can pass.

90jm7n.q: The sign shown warns in advance that you must give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction
90jm7n.why: This sign tells you to give way to vehicles approaching from the front, ahead of a stretch where the carriageway is narrowed.

1g6gpb0.q: The sign shown obliges you to give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction
1g6gpb0.why: This sign requires you to give way to oncoming vehicles at a narrowing or alternating one-way section (senso unico alternato) where only one line of vehicles can pass.

1le1j9i.q: The sign shown requires you to give way in alternating one-way sections
1le1j9i.why: This sign requires you to give way to oncoming vehicles at a narrowing or alternating one-way section (senso unico alternato) where only one line of vehicles can pass.

ld3sn9.q: The sign shown, on a two-way road, comes before a narrowing that allows only one line of vehicles to pass
ld3sn9.why: On a two-way road this sign comes before a narrowing (strettoia) where only one line of vehicles fits, so you must yield to oncoming traffic.

12vgz1.q: The sign shown warns that traffic cannot flow in both directions at the same time
12vgz1.why: The narrowing lets only one line of vehicles through, so traffic cannot run both ways at once and you must give way to oncoming vehicles.

1qutfk9.q: The sign shown is a regulatory (prescription) sign
1qutfk9.why: It is a regulatory sign (segnale di prescrizione) in the priority group: it orders a specific behaviour, giving way to oncoming vehicles.

328yro.q: The sign shown may be placed on a road where part of the carriageway is blocked
328yro.why: It may be placed where part of the carriageway is blocked, for example by roadworks, since only one line remains open and you must yield to oncoming vehicles.

1emmdqt.q: The sign shown may be placed on a road with a narrowing
1emmdqt.why: This sign requires you to give way to oncoming vehicles at a narrowing or alternating one-way section (senso unico alternato) where only one line of vehicles can pass.

5sz5ov.q: The sign shown requires you to give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction
5sz5ov.why: This sign requires you to give way to oncoming vehicles at a narrowing or alternating one-way section (senso unico alternato) where only one line of vehicles can pass.

1n70xgh.q: The sign shown prescribes giving way in alternating one-way sections
1n70xgh.why: This sign requires you to give way to oncoming vehicles at a narrowing or alternating one-way section (senso unico alternato) where only one line of vehicles can pass.

z7uoi4.q: The sign shown is found before a narrowing that normally allows only one line of vehicles to pass
z7uoi4.why: This sign requires you to give way to oncoming vehicles at a narrowing or alternating one-way section (senso unico alternato) where only one line of vehicles can pass.

6usnub.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we have priority if the light is green
6usnub.why: The traffic light overrides the sign: on green you may proceed and you have priority, with no need to give way to oncoming vehicles.

1nx8i0w.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we must give way if the light is off
1nx8i0w.why: When the light is off, the sign applies: you must give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

1sduuk0.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we have priority if the light is red but the traffic officer orders us to proceed
1sduuk0.why: A traffic officer's orders override both signs and lights: if the officer waves you through, you proceed and have priority.

1w4rgur.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we must give way if the light is flashing yellow
1w4rgur.why: A flashing yellow light does not settle priority, so the sign applies and you must give way to oncoming vehicles.

106zyqy.q: The sign shown warns that traffic is allowed in one direction on even days and in the other on odd days
106zyqy.why: The sign has nothing to do with alternate days: it requires you to give way to oncoming vehicles at a narrowing or alternating one-way section.

1yv0ctz.q: The sign shown warns of the right of way in alternating one-way sections
1yv0ctz.why: The sign requires you to give way; it does not grant priority. Priority in alternating sections has a different sign, with the red arrow in your direction.

189ryhm.q: The sign shown, on a one-way carriageway, warns of the start of two-way traffic
189ryhm.why: The sign requires you to give way to oncoming vehicles at a narrowing; it does not announce the start of two-way traffic.

8q737y.q: The sign shown warns of the end of the one-way system
8q737y.why: The sign requires you to give way to oncoming vehicles at narrowings; it does not mark the end of a one-way street.

16ebl58.q: The sign shown warns of the end of priority in alternating one-way sections
16ebl58.why: The sign requires you to give way to oncoming vehicles; it does not announce the end of any right of way.

1w7q4be.q: The sign shown is found on one-way roads
1w7q4be.why: The sign applies to narrowings on two-way roads, where oncoming vehicles meet you; it makes no sense on a one-way street.

icenrc.q: The sign shown is found before any narrowing of the carriageway
icenrc.why: It is used only for narrowings where one line of vehicles can pass; other narrowings have their own warning signs (restringimento di carreggiata).

1rjp56o.q: The sign shown is a prohibition sign
1rjp56o.why: It is a regulatory sign of the priority group, not a prohibition sign: it orders you to give way to oncoming vehicles.

wtggk1.q: The sign shown is placed at the start of a one-way street
wtggk1.why: The sign is placed before a narrowing on a two-way road, not at the start of a one-way street.

n0w1up.q: The sign shown obliges you, at intersections, to give way to vehicles coming from both the right and the left
n0w1up.why: The sign applies to narrowings and means yielding only to oncoming vehicles, not at intersections. Yielding from both sides is the YIELD (DARE PRECEDENZA) sign.

16xvjzp.q: The sign shown is a warning sign
16xvjzp.why: It is not a warning sign but a regulatory one: it is round with a red border and orders you to give way to oncoming vehicles.

1wwor02.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we must give way even if the light is green
1wwor02.why: On green the traffic light overrides the sign: you have priority and need not give way to oncoming vehicles.

4e1515.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we have priority if the light is flashing yellow
4e1515.why: On flashing yellow you do not have priority: the sign applies and you must give way to oncoming vehicles.

65qt7u.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we have priority if the light is green, but the traffic officer orders us to stop
65qt7u.why: The officer overrides lights and signs: if ordered to stop, you must stop and you have no priority at all.

vgk38w.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we must give way if the light is off and the traffic officer orders us to proceed
vgk38w.why: The officer's order overrides the sign: if the officer waves you through, you proceed without giving way to oncoming vehicles.

1b9k5gm.q: The sign shown calls for greater caution because there is no longer a right of way
1b9k5gm.why: The end of priority road sign (fine del diritto di precedenza) means the road no longer has priority: the general give-way-to-the-right rule applies again unless other signs say otherwise.

a9bm56.q: With the sign shown, the driver, unless another sign says otherwise, must give way to vehicles coming from the right
a9bm56.why: The end of priority road sign (fine del diritto di precedenza) means the road no longer has priority: the general give-way-to-the-right rule applies again unless other signs say otherwise.

96tvcw.q: The sign shown is a priority sign
96tvcw.why: It belongs to the priority signs, along with YIELD, STOP and priority road, and marks the end of priority.

d1592q.q: The sign shown indicates that the road no longer has right of way
d1592q.why: The end of priority road sign (fine del diritto di precedenza) means the road no longer has priority: the general give-way-to-the-right rule applies again unless other signs say otherwise.

125czkr.q: The sign shown may be followed by the sign STOP AND GIVE WAY
125czkr.why: After the end of priority, signs such as STOP AND GIVE WAY may follow to regulate the next intersections.

1le3j8h.q: The sign shown changes the previous rules on right of way at intersections
1le3j8h.why: The end of priority road sign (fine del diritto di precedenza) means the road no longer has priority: the general give-way-to-the-right rule applies again unless other signs say otherwise.

1a9bnqu.q: The sign shown indicates the restoration of the general rule on right of way
1a9bnqu.why: The end of priority road sign (fine del diritto di precedenza) means the road no longer has priority: the general give-way-to-the-right rule applies again unless other signs say otherwise.

135zac6.q: The sign shown indicates that a road with right of way ends
135zac6.why: The end of priority road sign (fine del diritto di precedenza) means the road no longer has priority: the general give-way-to-the-right rule applies again unless other signs say otherwise.

of5x68.q: The sign shown indicates that after it you will normally have to give way to the right
of5x68.why: The end of priority road sign (fine del diritto di precedenza) means the road no longer has priority: the general give-way-to-the-right rule applies again unless other signs say otherwise.

u5i0gv.q: The sign shown indicates the end of right of way on urban roads too
u5i0gv.why: The end of priority road sign (fine del diritto di precedenza) means the road no longer has priority: the general give-way-to-the-right rule applies again unless other signs say otherwise.

1pwdszk.q: The sign shown is an information sign
1pwdszk.why: It is a priority sign, not an information sign: the end of priority is a rule belonging to the priority group.

1oezcyv.q: The sign shown warns that you are travelling on a road with right of way
1oezcyv.why: It means the opposite: the road you are on loses its right of way. The plain yellow diamond (without the black bar) marks a priority road.

83zp.q: The sign shown obliges you to stop at the intersection
83zp.why: It does not require a stop: it only marks the end of priority. A stop is required by the STOP sign.

1vos54m.q: The sign shown indicates the layout of the main road
1vos54m.why: It does not show the course of the main road, but the end of priority (black bar across the yellow diamond).

5poy00.q: The sign shown always warns of an intersection with priority to the right
5poy00.why: It marks the end of priority, not necessarily an intersection: right-hand priority generally applies afterwards, but not always, since other signs may follow.

1rnhiue.q: The sign shown warns of the end of a previously imposed obligation
1rnhiue.why: It marks the end of the right of way, which is a right rather than an obligation, not the end of obligations in general.

qgeomx.q: The sign shown warns of a dead-end road
qgeomx.why: The sign does not indicate a dead end (strada senza uscita); it indicates the end of priority.

1ieyzlm.q: The sign shown indicates the end of a motorway
1ieyzlm.why: It does not mark the end of a motorway; it marks the end of priority. The end-of-motorway sign is a different, information sign.

1tthedk.q: The sign shown indicates the end of a one-way street
1tthedk.why: It indicates the end of priority, not the end of a one-way street.

1k67qjy.q: The sign shown indicates the end of a two-way road
1k67qjy.why: It indicates the end of priority, not the end of a two-way road.

94sx0w.q: The sign shown indicates the end of the speed limit
94sx0w.why: It indicates the end of priority; the end of a speed limit has a different sign, round with a diagonal bar.

18mz7en.q: The sign shown indicates the end of all prohibitions
18mz7en.why: It indicates the end of priority; the end of prohibitions is shown by a different sign, round with a diagonal bar.

wk351h.q: The sign shown warns of an intersection with less important roads
wk351h.why: The sign warns of an intersection with minor roads: whoever is on the main road has priority over vehicles coming from the side roads.

1xzp7d4.q: The sign shown warns of an intersection where you have priority over vehicles coming from the side roads
1xzp7d4.why: The sign warns of an intersection with minor roads: whoever is on the main road has priority over vehicles coming from the side roads.

1pzlakj.q: The sign shown warns of an intersection with a road without right of way
1pzlakj.why: The sign warns of an intersection with minor roads: whoever is on the main road has priority over vehicles coming from the side roads.

pqgeah.q: The sign shown, at the intersection, gives us priority over vehicles coming from both the right and the left
pqgeah.why: The sign warns of an intersection with minor roads: whoever is on the main road has priority over vehicles coming from the side roads.

1lvwrst.q: The sign shown loses its effect when a traffic officer is directing traffic
1lvwrst.why: A traffic officer's instructions override all signs: when an officer directs traffic, the sign has no effect.

tc9d9p.q: The sign shown may be preceded by the PRIORITY ROAD sign
tc9d9p.why: It can follow the PRIORITY ROAD (DIRITTO DI PRECEDENZA) sign, which marks the main road, ahead of intersections with minor roads.

1jxt74i.q: The sign shown warns that you should slow down to make sure priority is given to you
1jxt74i.why: Even with priority you need caution: slow down to check that vehicles from the side roads will let you pass.

18xumv9.q: The sign shown warns of an intersection where you have priority
18xumv9.why: The sign warns of an intersection with minor roads: whoever is on the main road has priority over vehicles coming from the side roads.

1ngc3yb.q: The sign shown warns of a merging road from both the right and the left
1ngc3yb.why: It does not warn of merging roads (confluenze) but of a crossroads with minor roads on both sides.

9l8694.q: The sign shown prohibits turning left at the intersection
9l8694.why: It is a warning sign, not a prohibition: it does not ban left turns but warns of an intersection with minor roads.

rnsos2.q: The sign shown warns of an intersection with priority over vehicles coming from the left, while you must give way to those coming from the right
rnsos2.why: You have priority over both side roads, right and left, not just one of them.

1lkk7x.q: The sign shown is placed on motorways
1lkk7x.why: Motorways have no level intersections, so this sign is not used there.

nnbl1z.q: The sign shown is placed no more than 25 metres from the intersection
nnbl1z.why: Warning signs stand further away, typically about 150 m outside built-up areas and less in town, not within 25 m.

tvjuus.q: The sign shown warns of an intersection where you must give way
tvjuus.why: At the intersection shown you have priority over vehicles on the side roads; you do not have to give way.

8s3p6r.q: The sign shown warns of acceleration lanes on the right and left
8s3p6r.why: The sign has nothing to do with acceleration lanes; it warns of an intersection with minor roads on the right and left.

1y9btoh.q: The sign shown warns that you will cross a less important road on the right
1y9btoh.why: The sign warns of a minor road joining from the right: you have priority on the main road, but caution is needed.

16qk066.q: The sign shown warns of an intersection with a side road joining from the right
16qk066.why: The sign warns of a minor road joining from the right: you have priority on the main road, but caution is needed.

vo4soc.q: With the sign shown you must be cautious because you are approaching an intersection
vo4soc.why: The sign warns of a minor road joining from the right: you have priority on the main road, but caution is needed.

10ya7aq.q: The sign shown is a priority sign
10ya7aq.why: The sign warns of a minor road joining from the right: you have priority on the main road, but caution is needed.

kebkxw.q: The sign shown warns of the intersection with a road without right of way
kebkxw.why: The sign warns of a minor road joining from the right: you have priority on the main road, but caution is needed.

127hafu.q: The sign shown warns of an intersection where the driver has priority over vehicles coming from the right
127hafu.why: The sign warns of a minor road joining from the right: you have priority on the main road, but caution is needed.

1w6akun.q: The sign shown warns of a dead-end road on the right
1w6akun.why: It does not indicate a dead end; it warns of an intersection with a minor road on the right.

72numn.q: The sign shown prohibits turning right
72numn.why: It is a warning sign, not a prohibition: it warns of an intersection with a minor road on the right.

au647z.q: The sign shown is placed on motorway acceleration lanes
au647z.why: It is not used on acceleration lanes: it warns of an intersection with a minor road on the right.

zl1zb8.q: The sign shown warns of a road merge with an acceleration lane
zl1zb8.why: It warns of an intersection with a minor road, not a merge with an acceleration lane, which has its own sign.

1lumrms.q: The sign shown warns of an intersection where the driver must stop and give way to vehicles coming from the right
1lumrms.why: It requires neither a stop nor giving way: you have priority over the minor road joining from the right.

pbzr99.q: The sign shown indicates a lay-by on the right
pbzr99.why: It does not indicate a lay-by (piazzola di sosta), which has an information sign; it warns of an intersection with a minor road on the right.

rsrfm0.q: The sign shown warns that a minor road crosses on the left
rsrfm0.why: This warning sign shows a side road joining from the left; the side road is the minor one and must yield.

17q40sz.q: The sign shown warns of a junction where you have right of way
17q40sz.why: You are on the main road, so traffic from the side road (strada laterale) must give way to you.

181ugbb.q: The sign shown requires you to use caution because you are approaching a junction
181ugbb.why: The sign warns of an upcoming junction and calls for caution, even though you have priority.

31kkch.q: The sign shown is a priority sign
31kkch.why: It belongs to the priority signs (segnali di precedenza): it warns of a junction where the side road must yield.

w2aihh.q: The sign shown warns of a junction with a road that has no right of way
w2aihh.why: The road joining from the left is the minor one and has no right of way.

u6s5g.q: The sign shown warns of a junction where you have priority over vehicles coming from the left
u6s5g.why: The side road on the left is minor, so its vehicles must give way to you on the main road.

ufcpe6.q: The sign shown warns of a dead-end road on the left
ufcpe6.why: The symbol does not mean a dead end; it shows a junction with a minor side road on the left.

1wqo8w6.q: The sign shown prohibits turning left
1wqo8w6.why: It is a warning sign and prohibits nothing; turn bans are circular red prohibition signs.

19japcp.q: The sign shown warns of a merge onto a motorway
19japcp.why: The sign shows a crossing with a side road on the left, not a merge or a motorway slip road.

ukshsm.q: The sign shown warns of a merge from the right
ukshsm.why: The side road is on the left and forms a crossing, not a merge from the right.

rdvtqk.q: The sign shown is placed on motorway entry ramps
rdvtqk.why: It warns of a junction with a minor road and is not used on motorway access ramps (rampe di accesso).

14l0fnc.q: The sign shown warns of a crossing with a siding
14l0fnc.why: The sign shows a junction with a minor road; rail crossings have different warning signs.

f59lz.q: The sign shown warns of a merge from the right with an acceleration lane
f59lz.why: The sign shows traffic merging from the right, using an acceleration lane (corsia di accelerazione).

xoyzq5.q: The sign shown warns of a merge on the right side
xoyzq5.why: The symbol shows a road merging into yours from the right.

16yu3ox.q: The sign shown can be found on motorways
16yu3ox.why: The merge warning sign is also used on motorways, near entry slip roads.

12rayh1.q: The sign shown calls for maximum caution to avoid accidents
12rayh1.why: It warns of vehicles merging from the right, so caution is needed to avoid accidents.

1r9vufe.q: The sign shown indicates that you have priority over vehicles merging from the right
1r9vufe.why: You are on the main road, so merging vehicles must give way to you.

1hi682t.q: With the sign shown, a GIVE WAY sign is placed on the connecting ramp
1hi682t.why: The merge sign implies that the connecting ramp (rampa di raccordo) carries a GIVE WAY sign.

5u81gb.q: The sign shown is placed no more than 25 metres from the junction
5u81gb.why: Warning signs are normally placed about 150 metres ahead outside built-up areas, not within 25 metres.

fb6sbz.q: The sign shown warns that you must give way to vehicles coming from the right
fb6sbz.why: You do not have to yield; vehicles merging from the right must give way to you.

1cy9a1x.q: The sign shown is placed on a secondary road that does not have right of way
1cy9a1x.why: It is placed on the main road, which has right of way, not on the secondary road.

1phehby.q: The sign shown can precede the GIVE WAY sign
1phehby.why: This sign is on the main road; the GIVE WAY sign is on the merging ramp, so it does not follow this sign.

1p7nw3w.q: On a motorway, the sign shown does not call for a reduction of speed
1p7nw3w.why: Even on a motorway a merge calls for caution, which means moderating your speed.

1y7ldnn.q: The sign shown allows turning right at the next junction
1y7ldnn.why: It is only a warning of a merge; it does not grant permission for any turn.

1m427bv.q: The sign shown warns of a merge with an acceleration lane on the left
1m427bv.why: The sign shows traffic merging from the left with an acceleration lane (corsia di accelerazione).

v5315e.q: The sign shown warns of a merge on the left side of the carriageway
v5315e.why: The symbol shows a road merging into the carriageway (carreggiata) from the left.

2ot9me.q: The sign shown is found on one-way carriageways
2ot9me.why: A merge from the left occurs on one-way carriageways, such as motorways.

171s8q9.q: The sign shown calls for caution because other vehicles may merge into the traffic flow
171s8q9.why: It warns that other vehicles may merge into the traffic, so caution is needed.

c7u8hg.q: The sign shown is used on roads with right of way
c7u8hg.why: It is used on the main road, which has right of way over the road that merges into it.

1924med.q: The sign shown implies a GIVE WAY sign on the side road joining the road
1924med.why: The merging side road carries a GIVE WAY sign.

izdj1e.q: The sign shown is placed no more than 25 metres from the junction
izdj1e.why: Warning signs are normally placed about 150 metres ahead outside built-up areas, not within 25 metres.

7yu68q.q: The sign shown requires you to give way to vehicles coming from the left
7yu68q.why: You have priority on the main road; the vehicles merging from the left must yield.

1e6n3aa.q: The sign shown warns that you do not have right of way at the merge
1e6n3aa.why: The vehicle on the main road has right of way at the merge.

k6fac.q: The sign shown precedes the GIVE WAY sign
k6fac.why: This sign is on the main road; the GIVE WAY sign is on the road that merges.

js546t.q: The sign shown, on motorways, precedes the mandatory left-turn sign
js546t.why: It warns of a merge from the left and does not precede a mandatory left-turn sign.

1rheviq.q: The sign shown allows turning left at the next junction
1rheviq.why: It is only a warning of a merge; it does not permit any turn.

1hjrlxd.q: The sign shown marks the start of a road where vehicles have right of way
1hjrlxd.why: The priority road sign marks the start of a road with right of way over side roads.

16bxzyf.q: The sign shown can be placed on a state road
16bxzyf.why: The priority road sign can be used on any main road, including a state road (strada statale).

96q8w3.q: With the sign shown you must still give way to vehicles with a flashing blue light and siren
96q8w3.why: Emergency vehicles with blue flashing lights and siren always have priority, even on a priority road.

10ucx3d.q: The sign shown is a priority sign
10ucx3d.why: It belongs to the priority signs (segnali di precedenza), together with STOP and GIVE WAY.

1b7mquo.q: With the sign shown you must still make sure that vehicles from side roads give way
1b7mquo.why: Even with right of way, you must check that vehicles from side roads actually yield.

17eouxx.q: The sign shown is a mandatory-instruction sign (segnale di prescrizione)
17eouxx.why: The priority road sign is a regulatory sign (segnale di prescrizione), like the other priority signs.

1f1q29p.q: The sign shown can be found at the start of an urban or rural road that has right of way
1f1q29p.why: It can mark the start of a priority road, whether urban or rural (extraurbana).

13dl8xy.q: The sign shown can be repeated in small size before and after each junction
13dl8xy.why: The sign may be repeated in a smaller size before and after each intersection.

1psh6gd.q: The sign in figure (A) can be repeated in small size and combined with the panel in figure (B)
1psh6gd.why: The priority road sign can be repeated in small size with a panel showing the layout of the priority road at the junction.

1c0nndo.q: The sign shown implies the presence of a GIVE WAY or STOP sign on the crossing roads
1c0nndo.why: The crossing roads must carry a GIVE WAY or STOP sign.

k7ucj6.q: With the sign shown you must still moderate your speed near junctions
k7ucj6.why: Even with right of way, you must slow down when approaching junctions.

1k0cj8c.q: The sign shown requires you to stop at the junction
1k0cj8c.why: It does not require a stop; only a STOP sign does that.

kljgk8.q: The sign shown can be placed to protect dangerous pedestrian crossings
kljgk8.why: It concerns right of way at junctions; pedestrian crossings have their own signs.

kskkpn.q: The sign shown is placed exclusively on rural roads with heavy traffic
kskkpn.why: It can be placed on urban or rural roads, with no restriction to heavy traffic.

xavr87.q: The sign shown warns of a junction with priority over vehicles coming from the right only
xavr87.why: It is not an advance warning and gives priority over all side roads, not only from the right.

gcourk.q: The sign shown warns of lanes reserved for public service buses
gcourk.why: It marks a priority road; bus lanes have different signs.

1as3y0t.q: The sign shown warns of the start of a road works site
1as3y0t.why: It marks a priority road; road works have their own warning signs.

1yoycnv.q: The sign shown is at the start of a road without right of way
1yoycnv.why: The sign marks the start of a road that does have right of way.

1q9at76.q: The sign shown is at the start of a motorway
1q9at76.why: A motorway start is shown by a specific blue or green sign; this one indicates right of way.

zfi0pp.q: The sign shown is found exclusively at the start of a state road
zfi0pp.why: It is used on any main road, not only state roads (strade statali).

1jbcd8y.q: With the sign shown no particular caution is needed because you have right of way
1jbcd8y.why: Caution is still needed because other drivers may fail to respect your priority.

1xssik.q: The sign shown is at the end of a road with right of way
1xssik.why: This sign marks the start of right of way; the end is shown by a sign with a diagonal black bar.

zfk2ih.q: The sign shown is at the end of a state road
zfk2ih.why: It marks a priority road, not the end of a state road.

1oc0jj5.q: The sign shown indicates that you have right of way until leaving the built-up area
1oc0jj5.why: Priority lasts until the end-of-priority sign, not until you leave the built-up area (centro abitato).

mzo0lx.q: With the sign shown you must check that oncoming vehicles give way to you
mzo0lx.why: The sign gives you priority, but you must make sure oncoming vehicles actually yield.

1x3s3q6.q: With the sign shown you may go through the narrowing after making sure you have been given priority
1x3s3q6.why: You have priority in the narrowing (strettoia), but proceed only after checking that oncoming vehicles yield.

15lntx0.q: With the sign shown you must proceed with caution, even if you have right of way
15lntx0.why: Even with priority, you must proceed carefully through the narrowing.

1y3ebz8.q: With the sign shown you can go through the narrowing after making sure oncoming vehicles have given way
1y3ebz8.why: You have priority, so go through the narrowing after checking that oncoming vehicles yield.

19v6fds.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic signal, you have priority if the light is green
19v6fds.why: The traffic light overrides the sign: on green you go, and the sign's priority applies.

hgozql.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic signal, you have priority if the signal is off
hgozql.why: When the signal is off, the sign applies and you have priority in the narrowing.

8kuk91.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic signal, you have priority if the light is red but the traffic officer orders you to go
8kuk91.why: A traffic officer's orders override signals and signs; if the officer waves you on, you have priority.

d5gbpn.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic signal, you must give way if the signal is off and the traffic officer orders you to stop
d5gbpn.why: The officer overrides signs and signals; if told to stop, you stop and give way.

1defpzq.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic signal, you have priority if the light is flashing yellow
1defpzq.why: Flashing yellow means the light is not controlling traffic, so the sign applies and you have priority.

xv2po8.q: With the sign shown you must give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction
xv2po8.why: The white arrow is your direction, which has priority; the red arrow must give way.

iyy22y.q: With the sign shown you may proceed without caution, since you have right of way
iyy22y.why: Even with priority in a narrowing, you must proceed with caution.

137q5ii.q: With the sign shown there are no particular obligations because the road is one-way
137q5ii.why: The road is two-way with an alternating one-way narrowing; it is not a one-way street.

yuut8m.q: With the sign shown two-way traffic begins
yuut8m.why: The sign regulates priority in a narrowing and does not mark the start of two-way traffic.

1h03vrb.q: With the sign shown you must be careful in the narrowing because traffic is two-way
1h03vrb.why: The sign gives priority in a narrowing; it does not announce two-way traffic.

1jzphe8.q: The sign shown warns of a ban on U-turns
1jzphe8.why: The sign gives priority in narrowings; U-turn bans have a different sign.

7508up.q: The sign shown warns of a ban on turning
7508up.why: The sign gives priority in narrowings and does not ban any turn.

1w5mfqh.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic signal, you have priority even if the light is red
1w5mfqh.why: On red the traffic light overrides the sign, so you must stop.

lwl2e0.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic signal, you must give way if the light is flashing yellow
lwl2e0.why: On flashing yellow the sign applies, and it gives you priority, so you need not yield.

vjm00k.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic signal, you have priority if the light is green and the traffic officer orders you to stop
vjm00k.why: The officer overrides lights and signs; if told to stop, you stop.

1wo9rh5.q: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic signal, you have priority if the signal is off and the traffic officer orders you to stop
1wo9rh5.why: The officer overrides the sign; if you are told to stop, you do not have priority.
